title: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors
notes: The dropout paper. Its central claim is a regularisation effect on a small MNIST network, which is close to ideal for reduced-scale testing: the mechanism is not scale dependent and the whole experiment fits on a CPU. The speech and object-recognition results depend on datasets that are not freely available.

claims.text: A feedforward network trained with 50% dropout on the hidden units makes fewer test errors on MNIST than the same network trained without dropout.
claims.notes: 160 errors without dropout, about 130 with. The core claim, and small enough to run on CPU.

claims.text: Also dropping out 20% of the input pixels reduces test error further compared to dropout on the hidden units alone.
claims.notes: 130 errors down to about 110. A difference of roughly 0.2 percentage points; at reduced scale with three seeds this is likely inside the noise.

claims.text: Dropout reduces the gap between training and test error, which the paper attributes to less co-adaptation between feature detectors.
claims.notes: The generalisation-gap framing of the same effect. This is the toy claim PLAN.md section 10 names.

claims.text: A network trained with dropout reaches about 110 test errors on MNIST.
Dropout lowers the frame classification error rate on the TIMIT speech benchmark relative to the same network without dropout.
claims.notes: TIMIT is licensed and not freely downloadable, so neither arm can be run here.

claims.text: Dropout improves error rates on CIFAR-10 relative to the same convolutional network without dropout.
claims.notes: Same mechanism on a dataset that is freely available and small enough to subsample.

claims.text: Dropout improves results on the ImageNet object recognition benchmark.
claims.notes: ImageNet-scale training is far outside a small CPU budget.
